Prealgebra · Lesson 7.2

Ratios with Many Parts

Solve this lesson →All lessons

A kombucha brewer keeps the same blend of tea, juice, and ginger every batch, writing it 6:4:16:4:1. Three quantities compared at once work exactly like a two-way ratio, with one more part.

Problem
A garden potting mix follows the ratio 5:3:25:3:2, compost to peat to sand. Using exactly one unscaled batch, how many scoops of potting mix is that in total?
Show a hint
  • A multi-way ratio like 5:3:25:3:2 names the actual amount of each part in one batch. So this batch really is 5 scoops of compost, 3 scoops of peat, and 2 scoops of sand.
  • Every scoop ends up in the same pile, so the total is just the parts of the ratio added together. Add 5+3+25+3+2.
Show the full solution
One unscaled batch is 5 scoops of compost, 3 scoops of peat, and 2 scoops of sand. Add them, 5+3+2=105+3+2=10, so the batch is 1010​ scoops. A ratio always carries a hidden total, the sum of its parts.
Problem
A marching band lines up in the ratio 5:3:15:3:1, brass to woodwinds to percussion. Reading the ratio in that order, how many parts belong to the woodwinds?
Show a hint
  • The labels are read in the same order as the numbers. The first number goes with brass, the second number goes with woodwinds, the third number goes with percussion. So which number sits in the woodwinds spot?
  • Line them up. Brass matches the 55, woodwinds matches the 33, and percussion matches the 11. The woodwinds part is the middle number.
Show the full solution
Read the labels in the same order as the numbers. Brass gets the 55, woodwinds gets the 33, and percussion gets the 11, so the woodwinds share is 33​ parts. In a multi-way ratio the position carries the meaning, so a number tells you nothing until you know which label it sits under.
Problem
A florist arranges roses to lilies to ferns in the ratio 3:2:43:2:4. What is the smallest total number of stems that fits this comparison exactly?
Show a hint
  • The three numbers 33, 22, 44 tell you the size of each share inside one full set. Add them up to see how many stems a single set of shares uses, then ask whether you could ever use fewer than that and still keep at least one of each.
  • One full set is 33 roses, 22 lilies, and 44 ferns. Bigger windows just stack more identical sets, so every valid total is a multiple of that one set's size. The smallest total is the size of a single set, which is why 88 cannot work.
Show the full solution
One full set of the ratio is 33 roses, 22 lilies, and 44 ferns, which is 3+2+4=93+2+4=9 stems. Any bigger arrangement just stacks more copies of that set, so every valid total is a multiple of 99. The smallest is one set, 99​ stems. Anything smaller cannot even hold one full set, so it cannot match the comparison.
Key idea
Multi-way ratios. A ratio can compare more than two quantities. a:b:ca:b:c compares three at once and is read “a to b to c.” The order matters, since it says which number belongs to which quantity. Like any ratio it fixes only the relative sizes, never the total. The real amounts could be a,b,ca,b,c, or twice each, or na:nb:ncna:nb:nc with one shared multiplier used on every part. So the total is always a multiple of a+b+ca+b+c.
Problem
A muralist mixes 18 oz blue, 12 oz white, and 30 oz black. Find the GCF of all three parts and write the simplified ratio of blue to white to black in the form a:b:c.
Show a hint
  • With a three-way ratio you reduce the same way you would a two-way one, except the factor has to divide every part at once. Ask what is the largest whole number that goes evenly into 1818, into 1212, and into 3030 all three.
  • List the factors of each part and hunt for the biggest one they share. 1818 splits as 6×36×3, 1212 as 6×26×2, and 3030 as 6×56×5, so the common factor is 66. Divide all three parts by 66.
Show the full solution
The largest number dividing 1818, 1212, and 3030 is 66, since 18=6×318=6×3, 12=6×212=6×2, and 30=6×530=6×5. Divide every part by 66 to get 3:2:53:2:5​. The factor has to divide all three parts, not just two of them, and 33, 22, 55 share nothing above 11, so this is fully reduced.
Problem
A board game ships action, coin, and gem tokens in the ratio 6:10:156:10:15. Write the ratio in lowest terms as a:b:c.
Show a hint
  • To simplify a multi-way ratio you cannot just look at two parts at a time. You need a number that divides into every part at once. Check each part: does 22 go into 66, 1010, and 1515? Does 33? Does 55? A factor only counts if it works for all three.
  • List the factors of each part. 6=2×36=2×3, 10=2×510=2×5, 15=3×515=3×5. The pairs each share something, but no single number divides all three. So the greatest common factor of all three is 11, and dividing every part by 11 changes nothing.
Show the full solution
Factor each part. 6=2×36=2×3, 10=2×510=2×5, and 15=3×515=3×5. Each pair shares something, but no number above 11 divides all three, so the greatest common factor is 11 and nothing reduces. The ratio stays 6:10:156:10:15​. A factor shared by two parts is not enough, it has to divide every part at once.
Problem
A baker\'s blend uses 113131​ cups oat flour, 22 cups rice flour, and 2332​ cup almond meal. Clear the fractions and reduce. Write the ratio of oat to rice to almond as a:b:c.
Show a hint
  • Every part is either a whole number or a number of thirds, so think about what single multiplier would turn all three into whole numbers at once. Multiplying every part by 33 does it, because 113=43131​=34​ and 2332​ both clear when tripled.
  • After scaling by 33 you get 4:6:24:6:2. Now find the greatest common factor of all three parts and divide every part by it to reach lowest terms.
Show the full solution
Write every part in thirds. Oat flour is 113=43131​=34​, rice flour is 2=632=36​, and almond meal is 2332​. Multiplying all three by 33 clears the denominators and gives 4:6:24:6:2. The greatest common factor of those is 22, so divide through to get 2:3:12:3:1​. Scaling every part by the same number never changes the comparison, so you can clear fractions first and reduce after.
Key idea
Simplest form. To reduce a multi-way ratio, divide every part by the greatest common factor that all the parts share, not a factor that divides only two of them. It is the same as reducing a fraction, applied to more numbers. You are done when no whole number above 11 divides every part at once. If the parts are fractions or mixed numbers, first multiply every part by a common denominator to turn them all into whole numbers, then reduce as usual.
Problem
A terrarium is layered sand to gravel to soil in the ratio 3:5:73:5:7, filling 60 scoops total. How many scoops of gravel does the terrarium use?
Show a hint
  • The ratio 3:5:73:5:7 means the 60 scoops are shared into 3+5+73+5+7 equal parts. Add those to find the total number of parts.
  • There are 1515 parts in all, so one part is 60÷1560÷15 scoops. Gravel is the 55 in the ratio, so it gets 55 of those parts.
Show the full solution
The ratio 3:5:73:5:7 splits the jar into 3+5+7=153+5+7=15 equal parts, so one part is 60÷15=460÷15=4 scoops. Gravel takes 55 parts, giving 5×4=205×4=20. The terrarium uses 2020​ scoops. Checking the rest, 12+20+28=6012+20+28=60, the full jar.
Problem
A choir keeps sopranos to altos to tenors in the ratio 6:5:46:5:4. Tonight 18 sopranos arrived. How many tenors are at the rehearsal?
Show a hint
  • The sopranos hold the soprano part of the comparison, which is 6. So 18 sopranos fill up 6 equal parts. Divide to find what just one part is worth, then remember the tenors hold 4 of those same parts.
  • One part is 18÷6=318÷6=3 singers. Tenors take the 44 part, so multiply 4×34×3.
Show the full solution
Sopranos hold the 66 in 6:5:46:5:4, and 18 sopranos fill those 66 parts, so one part is 18÷6=318÷6=3 singers. Tenors hold 44 parts, so there are 4×3=124×3=12​ tenors. You never need the choir total here. Once one part is known, every section scales from it.
Problem
An orchard plants apple to pear to plum in the ratio 4:3:24:3:2. This season there are 24 plum trees. How many trees are in the whole orchard?
Show a hint
  • The plum trees are the 22 part of the ratio 4:3:24:3:2. So those 2424 plum trees are spread evenly across 22 equal parts. Divide to find what just one part is worth.
  • One part is 24÷2=1224÷2=12 trees. Now count how many parts the whole orchard has, 4+3+24+3+2, and multiply that many parts by 1212.
Show the full solution
Plums are the 22 in 4:3:24:3:2, so the 24 plum trees fill 22 parts and one part is 24÷2=1224÷2=12 trees. The whole orchard is 4+3+2=94+3+2=9 parts, so it holds 9×12=1089×12=108​ trees. Checking, 48+36+24=10848+36+24=108.
Key idea
Parts method with many shares. Read a:b:ca:b:c as a+b+ca+b+c equal parts. Add every number to get the part count, then divide the real total by that count to find what one part is worth. Each quantity is its own part count times that one-part value. The method is the same whether there are two, three, or more shares.

Sometimes you get two ratios that share a quantity, like A:BA:B and B:CB:C, and you want all three in one ratio a:b:ca:b:c. The trouble is that the shared quantity usually shows up as a different number in each ratio, so they do not line up. The fix is to scale each ratio until both give the shared quantity the same number, and then the two snap together into one.

Problem
In a gear train, front to middle is 4:34:3 and middle to rear is 2:52:5. Rescale so the middle numbers match, then write front to rear as a:b in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • The middle gear is counted as 33 in the first ratio and 22 in the second. To stitch the two ratios together you need the middle number to be the same in both. Pick a common multiple of 33 and 22, and 66 is the smallest one.
  • Scale 4:34:3 up by 22 to get 8:68:6, and scale 2:52:5 up by 33 to get 6:156:15. Now both say 66 for the middle, so line them up as front to middle to rear and look at just the front and rear numbers.
Show the full solution
The middle gear reads 33 in 4:34:3 and 22 in 2:52:5, so scale both until the middle is 66. Doubling the first gives 8:68:6, and tripling the second gives 6:156:15. The chain is 8:6:158:6:15, front to middle to rear, so front to rear is 8:158:15​, already in lowest terms. The shared gear is the hinge. Once its number matches in both ratios, the two comparisons join into one.
Key idea
Linking two ratios through a shared part. When A:BA:B and B:CB:C name the same middle quantity BB but give different numbers for it, scale each ratio until both show the same BB. That shared value is usually a common multiple of the two BB values. Once the numbers agree, write the three quantities as one ratio A:B:CA:B:C. From it you can read any comparison, including A:CA:C, which neither original ratio gave.
Fun fact
A major chord\'s notes vibrate near 4:5:64:5:6. The root-to-fifth gives 4:6=3:24:6=3:2, the "perfect fifth." Since 4, 5, 6 share no common factor, 4:5:64:5:6 is already in lowest terms.
Problem
Yellow to blue is 3:23:2 and blue to white is 4:74:7. Rescale so the blue numbers agree, then write the ratio of yellow to white as a:b in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Blue is 22 in the first ratio and 44 in the second. To make them match, double everything in the first ratio so its blue becomes 44. What does 3:23:2 become when you double both parts?
  • After doubling, yellow to blue is 6:46:4 and blue to white is 4:74:7. The blue 44 is now the same in both, so stack them into one chain 6:4:76:4:7. Read off just the yellow and the white parts, then reduce.
Show the full solution
Blue is 22 in 3:23:2 and 44 in 4:74:7, so double the first ratio to get 6:46:4. Both now call blue 44, and the chain is 6:4:76:4:7, yellow to blue to white. Yellow to white is 6:76:7​, already in lowest terms. Doubling both parts leaves the comparison unchanged, which is what lets the two ratios line up.
Problem
In a sourdough recipe, flour to water is 5:35:3, water to starter is 6:56:5. Water appears as 3 in one and 6 in the other. Rescale and combine. How many grams of flour are in a 630-gram batch?
Show a hint
  • The water amount is 3 in the first ratio and 6 in the second. Rescale one ratio so both read the same number for water. Doubling 5:35:3 gives 10:610:6, which now matches the 66 in the water to starter ratio, so you can stitch them into one flour to water to starter ratio.
  • Once the three-way ratio is 10:6:510:6:5, add the parts to see how many equal shares the 630630 grams splits into, find what one share weighs, then take the flour parts.
Show the full solution
Water reads 33 in 5:35:3 and 66 in 6:56:5, so double the first ratio to 10:610:6. The chain is 10:6:510:6:5, flour to water to starter, which is 10+6+5=2110+6+5=21 parts. One part is 63021=3021630​=30 grams, and flour is 1010 parts, so the batch has 10×30=30010×30=300​ grams of flour. Checking, 300+180+150=630300+180+150=630.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A birdseed recipe follows the ratio 7:4:27:4:2, millet to sunflower to cracked corn. Using exactly one unscaled batch, how many parts of birdseed are there in total?
Show the solution
One unscaled batch is 77 parts millet, 44 parts sunflower, and 22 parts cracked corn. Add them, 7+4+2=137+4+2=13​ parts. Unscaled means you use the ratio numbers exactly as written, with no multiplier.
Practice
A printmaker logs a blend as 20:50:3520:50:35, cyan to magenta to yellow. Divide every part by the GCF of all three. Write the simplified ratio in the form a:b:c.
Show the solution
The factors of 2020 are 1,2,4,5,10,201,2,4,5,10,20, of 5050 are 1,2,5,10,25,501,2,5,10,25,50, and of 3535 are 1,5,7,351,5,7,35. The largest on all three lists is 55, so divide every part by 55 to get 4:10:74:10:7​. Since 77 is prime and divides neither 44 nor 1010, there is nothing left to divide out.
Practice
A trail mix uses oats, raisins, and seeds in the ratio 10:9:2510:9:25. Reduce to lowest terms, if nothing divides all three, the original is the answer. Write your answer as a:b:c.
Show the solution
Start with 99, the most restrictive part. It is odd, so 22 is out, and its only other factors are 33 and 99, neither of which divides 1010. So the greatest common factor of 1010, 99, and 2525 is 11 and nothing reduces. The ratio stays 10:9:2510:9:25​.
Practice
A flower farmer counts 42 marigolds, 14 basil plants, and 28 thyme plants. Simplify the ratio 42:14:2842:14:28 to lowest terms. Write as a:b:c.
Show the solution
The factors of 1414 are 1,2,7,141,2,7,14, and 1414 itself divides the others, since 42=14×342=14×3 and 28=14×228=14×2. Divide every part by 1414, keeping the order marigolds, basil, thyme, and you get 3:1:23:1:2​. Checking the smallest part first is a shortcut, since the greatest common factor can never be bigger than it.
Practice
A smoothie uses 1331​ cup mango, 1661​ cup spinach, and 1221​ cup yogurt. Clear fractions with a common denominator and reduce. Write the ratio as a:b:c.
Show the solution
The denominators are 3, 6, and 2, and 6 is the smallest number all three divide into. Multiply every part by 6, giving 13×6=231​×6=2, 16×6=161​×6=1, and 12×6=321​×6=3. That is 2:1:32:1:3​, and 2, 1, and 3 share no factor above 1. Multiplying every part by the same number keeps the comparison the same, so clearing fractions costs you nothing.
Practice
A candle recipe uses 212221​ oz soy wax, 114141​ oz beeswax, and 5885​ oz fragrance oil. Clear fractions, then reduce. Write the ratio as a:b:c in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Every part is a number of eighths, so multiply all three by 8. Soy wax gives 212×8=20221​×8=20, beeswax gives 114×8=10141​×8=10, and fragrance oil gives 58×8=585​×8=5. The greatest common factor of 2020, 1010, and 55 is 55, so divide through to get 4:2:14:2:1​. Clear the fractions first, then reduce, and every step stays in whole numbers.
Practice
A mosaic border of 96 tiles uses gold, copper, and slate in the ratio 1:2:51:2:5. How many copper tiles are in the border?
Show the solution
The ratio 1:2:51:2:5 splits the border into 1+2+5=81+2+5=8 equal parts, so one part is 96÷8=1296÷8=12 tiles. Copper is the 22, so it takes 2×12=242×12=24​ tiles. Checking, 12+24+60=9612+24+60=96, the whole border.
Practice
A 75-bead bracelet uses jade, amber, onyx, and pearl in the ratio 2:4:3:62:4:3:6. How many pearl beads are on the bracelet?
Show the solution
Add the parts, 2+4+3+6=152+4+3+6=15, so one share is 75÷15=575÷15=5 beads. Pearl holds 66 shares, giving 6×5=306×5=30​ pearl beads. Four shares work exactly like three. The only change is that you add one more number at the start.
Practice
A robotics club has builders, coders, and designers in the ratio 8:5:38:5:3. Tonight 35 coders showed up. How many builders does the club have?
Show the solution
Coders hold 55 parts, and 35 coders fill them, so one part is 35÷5=735÷5=7 members. Builders hold 88 parts, so the club has 8×7=568×7=56​ builders. Once one part is known, every group scales from it, and you never need the club total.
Practice
A produce crate is packed plums to apples to pears in the ratio 2:9:42:9:4. The crate holds 28 pears. How many apples are in the crate?
Show the solution
In the comparison 2:9:42:9:4 the pears are the third number, so they are worth 4 parts. The crate holds 28 pears, and those 28 pears fill 4 equal parts, so one part is 28÷4=728÷4=7 pieces of fruit. Now look at the apples. They are the middle number, worth 9 parts. Each part is 7, so the apples come to 9×7=639×7=63. That gives 6363​.
Practice
A relay team splits training as run to bike to swim to row in the ratio 6:5:4:36:5:4:3. The bike leg is 20 km. How many kilometers is the whole training distance?
Show the solution
The bike leg is the 55 in 6:5:4:36:5:4:3, and 20 km fills those 55 parts, so one part is 20÷5=420÷5=4 km. The whole distance covers 6+5+4+3=186+5+4+3=18 parts, so it is 18×4=7218×4=72​ kilometers.
Practice
A spice jar blends cumin, paprika, and chili in the ratio 7:2:17:2:1. The jar has 18 grams of paprika. How many grams of spice are in the jar altogether?
Show the solution
Paprika is the 22 in 7:2:17:2:1, and 18 grams fills those 2 parts, so one part is 18÷2=918÷2=9 grams. The whole jar is 7+2+1=107+2+1=10 parts, so it holds 10×9=9010×9=90​ grams. Checking, 63+18+9=9063+18+9=90.
Practice
A clockwork toy has three gears. Gear 1 to gear 2 turns at 5:65:6. Gear 2 to gear 3 turns at 4:34:3. Rescale so the gear-2 numbers match, then write gear 1 to gear 3 as a:b in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Gear 2 reads 66 in 5:65:6 and 44 in 4:34:3, and both divide 1212. Scale 5:65:6 by 22 to get 10:1210:12, and scale 4:34:3 by 33 to get 12:912:9. The chain is 10:12:910:12:9, so gear 1 to gear 3 is 10:910:9​, already in lowest terms.
Practice
Nitrogen to phosphorus is 2:32:3 and phosphorus to potash is 9:89:8. Rescale the first ratio so its phosphorus matches 9, combine, then write nitrogen to potash as a:b in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Phosphorus reads 33 in 2:32:3 and 99 in 9:89:8, so multiply the first ratio by 33 to get 6:96:9. The chain is 6:9:86:9:8, nitrogen to phosphorus to potash, so nitrogen to potash is 6:86:8, which divides by 22 down to 3:43:4​. Reduce at the end, after you have pulled out the two parts you actually want.

Learn it by doing it

Reading is a start. In the course you solve each problem yourself, with instant feedback, layered hints, and Milo right beside you when you get stuck.
